newsitem.title: USA: UBS ups Peru, Argentina, trims Mexico in portfolio.
newsitem.headline: UBS ups Peru, Argentina, trims Mexico in portfolio.

text.p: UBS Securities said Wednesday it had raised its allocations for Argentina and Peru in its model portfolio of Latin American stocks and cut its allocation for Mexico.
In a May 21 report, analyst Lawrence Krohn he had raised his rating for Argentina to overweight from neutral and for Peru to overweight from underweight.
He also cut Mexico to neutral from overweight.
Krohn said he cut Mexico's weighting because of "sustained weakness in consumer sector, which threatens to sap momentum of heretofore impressive recovery.
"First-quarter earnings disappointing, but excellent opportunities remain in selected sectors."
Mexico's portion of the portfolio went to 27.3 percent from 33.4 percent.
Argentina's weighting change was based on "solid diversified recovery and diminished risk of damage inflicted by U.S. market developments.
"Many institution are still underweight. The Merval (the Buenos Aires stock exchange) remains expensive."
Argentina went to 12 percent from 11.5 percent of the portfolio.
Krohn said his shift on Peru stemmed from a "burgeoning recovery whose sustainability has been enhanced by progress on inflation and trade fronts. Market still attractively priced."
Peru weighting went to 3.5 percent from 2.5 percent.
Brazil remained overweight, Chile and Colombia stayed underweight and Venezuela was kept neutral.
